title: DT-TEO canonical message (v2)
description: The one message shape every service after the ingestion gateway receives. One message = one reading of one point. Meaning (what the point is, what it belongs to) lives in the asset model, linked by `point`. A reading is identified by `site` + `point` (like SenML, RFC 8428 section 4.2, where base name + name must be globally unique). v2 (step 2i) added `site`, `time_source` and `qc`; see contracts/NOTES.md.

v.description: Schema version. Bump when the shape changes so old and new messages can be told apart.

site.description: Which site the reading belongs to (from gateway config; the same value as the {site} level in the topic). Together with `point` it makes the reading's identity unique across sites.

point.description: Point ID. Must match a ref:hasTimeseriesId in the asset model (dtteo_asset_model.ttl). Lowercase, dot-separated: <equipment>.<point>. Unique within a site, not across sites.

value.description: The reading after normalisation. Numbers for measurements and percentages, strings for modes/states, booleans for on/off.

unit.description: QUDT unit ID, the same one used by brick:hasUnit in the asset model (e.g. DEG_C, KiloW, PERCENT). null for values with no unit, such as a mode.

sensor_time.description: When the reading was measured (event time), in UTC. If the source gives no time, the gateway uses the time it received the value; `time_source` then says "gateway".

ingest_time.description: When the ingestion gateway received the reading (processing time), in UTC. Always set by the gateway, never by the device.

time_source.description: Who set sensor_time. "device" = the device's own clock. "gateway" = the device sent no time, so sensor_time is the arrival time (SenML treats a missing time as 'roughly now', RFC 8428 section 4.5.3). Gateway-stamped readings are less precise in time, and an MQTT QoS 1 re-delivery of one can't be recognised as a duplicate by its time.

quality.description: Set by the validator. GOOD = passed all checks. SUSPECT = usable but flagged (e.g. outside the usual range, or arrived late). BAD = failed a check; stored for the record but not used by the twin.

qc.description: Only present when quality is not GOOD: each check that flagged the reading, so the reason is stored with the data rather than only in the gateway log. Follows QARTOD practice of keeping a flag per test (ioos_qc).

source.description: Optional. Where the reading came from, as <adapter>:<device id>. Used for tracing problems back to a device.
